title: Anaemia: the three patterns and the first tests

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on standard haematology teaching and the BSG and ASH guidance on iron deficiency. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: Which single test best separates under-production from loss or destruction of red cells?
questions.why: A low reticulocyte response means the marrow is not keeping up; a high one means it is responding to bleeding or haemolysis. The mean cell volume then sorts the low producers.

questions.q: Below what ferritin is iron deficiency confirmed regardless of other tests?
questions.why: Ferritin rises with inflammation, so a value up to 100 can still hide iron deficiency in a patient with an inflammatory illness; a low transferrin saturation helps there.

questions.q: A 62-year-old man has iron deficiency anaemia and no obvious source. What does he need?
d: Oral iron and a recheck in 3 months
A faecal occult blood test first
Nothing further if he feels well
questions.why: In men and postmenopausal women iron deficiency is gastrointestinal blood loss until proven otherwise. Coeliac serology is sent at the same time.

questions.q: How is oral iron best dosed for absorption?
questions.a: A single dose every other day
d: Three times a day with meals
questions.why: A dose raises hepcidin for about a day and blocks the next one. Alternate-day dosing absorbs as much iron with fewer gut side effects.

questions.q: By about how much should haemoglobin rise after 2 to 4 weeks of oral iron if it is working?
questions.why: No rise means the diagnosis, the adherence or the absorption is wrong. Treatment continues for three months after the haemoglobin normalises to refill the stores.

questions.q: Which are causes of a macrocytic anaemia?
questions.why: Folate deficiency, liver disease and myelodysplasia complete the common list. Hypersegmented neutrophils on the film point to B12 or folate.

questions.q: A B12 level is borderline low in a patient with numbness in the feet. Which test confirms deficiency?
questions.why: Methylmalonic acid rises in B12 deficiency but not in folate deficiency, whereas homocysteine rises in both. Neurological symptoms can precede the anaemia.

questions.q: Why is folate not given alone to a patient with an unexplained macrocytic anaemia?
questions.a: It can correct the anaemia while B12 deficiency continues to damage the nervous system
d: It raises the risk of thrombosis
questions.why: B12 is checked, or given alongside, before folate. High-dose oral B12 of 1000 micrograms works even in pernicious anaemia, though injections are still often used.

questions.q: Which findings point to haemolysis as the cause of an anaemia?
d: A raised mean cell volume alone
questions.why: A blood film and a direct antiglobulin test come next to separate immune from mechanical and inherited causes.

questions.q: A microcytic anaemia with a normal ferritin, a high red cell count and a Mentzer index under 13. What does that suggest?
questions.why: Iron is not given, since these patients are not iron deficient. Haemoglobin electrophoresis confirms beta thalassaemia trait; alpha trait needs genetic testing.

questions.q: In anaemia of chronic kidney disease, what is corrected before an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent is considered?
questions.why: Iron is replaced when transferrin saturation is under 30% and ferritin under 500. The stimulating agent is added when haemoglobin is under 10 and other causes are excluded.

questions.q: In a stable hospitalised patient without cardiac disease, below what haemoglobin is transfusion recommended?
questions.why: A restrictive threshold is as safe as a liberal one in most settings. A threshold of 8 is used for cardiac surgery and existing cardiovascular disease.
